mathematical_or_operational_scope: Five-parameter determinant circuit H after eliminating beta on B(h)!=0 and eliminating gamma1,gamma2 through a 3x3 coefficient determinant.
positive_controls: Lines 25–33 enforce gamma linearity and beta degree at most two; lines 60–61 enforce internally constructed 3x3x3 dimensions.

Lines 42–55 homogenize each matrix entry by B^2, and lines 73–85 compare H with B^6 times the beta-substituted determinant. The fixed nonzero witness proves H is not identically zero, provided the coefficient arithmetic is correct.

findings.issue: Random beta-substitution tests skip B=0 and do not assert a positive successful count for each embedding. The hard-coded witness tests a separate point.

H=0 is a necessary homogeneous compatibility condition only. A nullspace of the 3x3 matrix need not contain a vector with first coordinate 1; it does not guarantee finite gamma1,gamma2, a solution of original equations, or all regularity guards.
degree_upper_bound=36 is metadata, not recomputed/asserted in this file. It is a conservative bound from degree arithmetic, not a measured minimal degree.
B(h)=0 and earlier endpoint/corner exceptional loci remain. Polynomial nonvanishing at one point is not infeasibility or generic existence of the required factorization.

cost_and_scaling: Avoids fully expanding a potentially high-degree determinant by storing exact sparse coefficient polynomials and a constant-size determinant circuit. Reconstructing coefficients still performs exact_upper and exact_minor work; this is not a fast Fourier application routine.
test_scope_and_limits: Up to 120 usable random homogeneity comparisons across two primes and two roots, plus one fixed modular nonzero witness. Read only. No consumer-side schema validation or end-to-end candidate reconstruction.
certificate_acceptance: Useful necessary condition with a clearly bounded patch. Exported coefficient circuit is structurally well formed by construction, but the independent consumer’s zip-based checks do not fully validate hostile/malformed saved coefficients.
